proposed: The question we came with gets its answer. At least 9.0% of words in current legislative speech are machine-drafted — a floor, because directed effort evades the detector. The share spreads fourfold across chambers and concentrates in scripted genres, with no quality penalty: against a deliberation rubric, flagged speech is better-formed and no less engaged, in the cross-chamber arm and in controlled model continuations alike.
rationale: The stress position (principle 3): the original is one sentence whose syntactic closure lands on 'controlled model continuations alike,' so the 9.0% floor and the quality result never receive end-weight. Three sentences give each claim its own closure — the floor, then the spread-and-quality package — without adding or dropping a datum.
